name: mycrew
description: A five-layer harness for Claude Code, each layer driving the one below: primitives and house rules, a pipeline that carries a task from decision to hardened code, a product plane holding what the product must do, a board holding what is being done about it right now, and the crew that builds it — a chief over the whole product, a lead to a feature, a worker to an assignment. Beside the layers stand the specialists, a plugin each and only where the trade is substantial enough to earn one: agent-designer decides how the product looks and settles it by building it, agent-warden keeps the board honest. Install mycrew-tools first.

plugins.name: mycrew-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/5 — the primitives. Small, project-agnostic skills you reach for mid-work: /slap resets a fix that has stopped working, /likec4 draws architecture as code, /reminder pins a rule as a hard constraint, /retract hunts down information declared wrong and cuts it out. Ships the house rule files too. Everything above builds on this.

plugins.name: mycrew-pipeline
plugins.description: Layer 2/5 — the build pipeline. Six stages carry one task from a decision to shipped code: /how-to-do settles the fork, /do builds it, then /refactor, /review, /secure and /test harden it. In review and secure, the eyes that hunt are never the author's. Every stage weighs what actually changed and skips in one honest line when the change doesn't earn it.

plugins.name: mycrew-product
plugins.description: Layer 3/5 — the product plane: everything true about the whole product, above the sub-projects. /product-init founds it. /braindump and /ask-me draw the product out of you and file each piece where it belongs; /propose-idea is the one that puts an idea in, and only on your approval. Whatever you affirm, wherever you affirm it, product-rules is the one rule set that decides where it lands and in what shape.

plugins.name: mycrew-board
plugins.description: Layer 4/5 — the board: what is being done right now about what the plane says the product must be. Built on backlog.md, so tasks are plain markdown in the repo and the same board opens in a terminal or a browser. The board belongs to the leads — the chief speaks to them in words and workers answer in reports, and neither writes a card. Every card records whose requirement it is rather than whose hand wrote it, and a card nobody asked for is gated before a worker is ever spent on it. /board-init stands the board up over the features the plane already holds; board-rules governs what a card carries and who may move it.

plugins.name: mycrew-crew
plugins.description: Layer 5/5 — the crew: the ones who actually build the product. Three characters, each handing down to the next. The chief is your deputy over the whole product, one to a product, owning the plane and delegating each approved feature whole. A lead holds one feature across every repo it touches, spawned as a background session of its own and reaching the other leads only where its feature depends on theirs. A worker carries one assignment end to end through the pipeline and hands back a four-field report. Each carries how it runs the rung below, so there is nothing to load and nothing to forget. Only the worker writes code.

plugins.name: agent-designer
plugins.description: A specialist, not a layer — the trade that decides how the product looks. A lead dispatches @designer exactly as it dispatches a worker and gets back the same four fields, but what comes back is a running interface: it founds a visual language where none exists and extends one where it does, and it never leaves a mockup behind. It carries the whole trade inside itself — what a good look is, what a machine-made one is and the defaults that mark it, what the words on a surface must do, and the floor nothing ships below.

plugins.name: agent-warden
plugins.description: A specialist, not a layer — the keeper of the board. It wakes on every change a card makes and checks the one thing nothing else can: that the rules the crew works by actually held. Agent-born work in progress that never passed the gate, a card serving no feature, a card closed with its criteria still unchecked, one in progress that no live worker holds, one untouched for days — it asks the lead who owns it, and only flags what was already asked about and broken again. It never judges the work, never writes a card, and never says how anything should be built. /warden-stop and /warden-start put the watch down and pick it up without losing the session; every wake leaves a line on disk, so the whole watch reads back afterwards.
